title: MATH 12-01 Mastery Challenge: Matrices: Definitions, J.J. Sylvester, Matrix Taxonomy, Trace & Triangular Forms

questions.promptText: What is the trace of the matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & -2 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 & 7 \\ 0 & 9 & -6 \end{bmatrix}$?
In what year and by which mathematician was the word "matrix" introduced into mathematical literature?
questions.explanation: James Joseph Sylvester introduced the term 'matrix' in 1850.

questions.promptText: What is the multiplicative inverse (reciprocal) of $z = 1 + j2$?
What type of matrix is a square matrix whose entries above the main diagonal are all ZERO?
questions.explanation: A lower triangular matrix has non-zero entries only on and below the main diagonal ($a_{ij} = 0$ for $i < j$).

questions.promptText: What type of matrix is $S = \begin{bmatrix} 7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 7 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 \end{bmatrix}$?
questions.explanation: A diagonal matrix with identical entries $k$ along its main diagonal is a scalar matrix ($7I$).

questions.promptText: If $2x + j3y = 8 - j12$, what are the real values of $x$ and $y$?
questions.explanation:
Equating real parts: $2x = 8 \implies x = 4$. Equating imaginary parts: $3y = -12 \implies y = -4$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $x = 8/2 = 4, y = -12/3 = -4$.

questions.promptText: What are the dimensions (size) of a column vector with 5 rows?
questions.explanation: Dimensions are always given as $m \times n$ (rows $\times$ columns). A 5-row column vector is $5 \times 1$.

questions.promptText: Find the trace of the $4 \times 4$ identity matrix $I_4$.
questions.explanation:
$\text{tr}(I_4) = 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 4$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $\text{tr}(I_n) = n = 4$.

questions.promptText: What is the leading entry in the matrix row $[0, 0, 7, -3, 2]$?
questions.explanation: The leading entry of a row is the first non-zero entry from the left, which is 7.

questions.promptText: Find the reciprocal of $z = -j4$.
questions.explanation:
$\frac{1}{-j4} = \frac{j}{-j^2 4} = \frac{j}{4} = j 0.25$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $\frac{1}{-j} = j \implies \frac{j}{4} = j0.25$.

questions.promptText: What is an Upper Triangular Matrix?
questions.choiceA: A square matrix in which all elements below the main diagonal are zero ($a_{ij} = 0$ for $i > j$)
questions.choiceB: A matrix with entries above the diagonal equal to zero
questions.choiceD: A matrix where all diagonal entries are zero
questions.explanation: An upper triangular matrix has non-zero entries on and above the main diagonal.

questions.promptText: Find the trace of the matrix $B = \begin{bmatrix} -3 & 8 & 1 \\ 0 & 5 & -4 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$.
questions.explanation:
$\text{tr}(B) = -3 + 5 + 2 = 4$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $-3 + 5 + 2 = 4$.

questions.promptText: If $A$ is a $3 \times 4$ matrix and $B$ is a $4 \times 2$ matrix, what are the dimensions of the product matrix $A B$?
questions.explanation: Matrix multiplication $(m \times k)(k \times n)$ results in an $m \times n$ matrix, so $(3 \times 4)(4 \times 2) = 3 \times 2$.

questions.promptText: Which matrix is a Diagonal Matrix?
questions.explanation: A diagonal matrix has non-zero entries exclusively along its main diagonal ($a_{ij} = 0$ for $i \ne j$).

questions.promptText: Find the reciprocal of $z = 4 - j3$.
What property characterizes a Null (Zero) Matrix $O$?
questions.choiceA: Every single element of the matrix is equal to zero ($a_{ij} = 0$)
questions.choiceB: Only the diagonal elements are zero
questions.choiceD: It must be a square matrix
questions.explanation: A null matrix consists entirely of zero entries and can have any dimension $m \times n$.

questions.promptText: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2k & 3 \\ -1 & k+4 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\text{tr}(A) = 16$, find $k$.
questions.explanation:
$\text{tr}(A) = 2k + (k + 4) = 3k + 4 = 16 \implies 3k = 12 \implies k = 4$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $3k = 12 \implies k = 4$.

questions.promptText: What is the Identity Matrix property for any compatible square matrix $A$?
questions.explanation: The identity matrix $I$ acts as the multiplicative identity in matrix algebra ($A I = I A = A$).

questions.promptText: What is a single row matrix $[a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n]$ formally termed?
questions.choiceA: Row Vector (or Row Matrix of size $1 \times n$)
questions.explanation: A matrix containing a single row is called a row matrix or row vector.

questions.promptText: Find the trace of the diagonal matrix $D = \text{diag}(10, -4, 2, 7)$.
If $(x + y) + j(x - y) = 10 + j4$, find $x$ and $y$.
questions.explanation:
$x + y = 10$ and $x - y = 4$. Adding: $2x = 14 \implies x = 7$. Subtracting: $2y = 6 \implies y = 3$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $x = (10+4)/2 = 7, y = (10-4)/2 = 3$.

questions.promptText: What is the relationship between the trace of a square matrix and its eigenvalues $\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \dots, \lambda_n$?
questions.choiceA: The trace equals the SUM of the eigenvalues: $\text{tr}(A) = \sum_{i=1}^n \lambda_i$
questions.choiceB: The trace equals the product of the eigenvalues
questions.choiceC: The trace is independent of the eigenvalues
questions.choiceD: The trace equals the maximum eigenvalue
questions.explanation: A fundamental invariant of linear algebra is that $\text{tr}(A) = \sum \lambda_i$ (while $\det(A) = \prod \lambda_i$).
